title: Python SDK: stream resume + event splitter and filtering patterns
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal:
Implement a Python SDK pattern that makes handling streaming chat completions ergonomic for real-world apps: support resuming interrupted streams, splitting raw event sequences into typed events, and providing easy filtering hooks for middleware. This ticket delivers the reference implementation, examples, unit tests, and a short migration guide for current users of the StreamingChat API.

Background:
We continue to see customer reports where network blips (proxy resets, ephemeral infra preemption) cause in-progress streaming chat requests to fail. Some customers need the ability to resume from a stable checkpoint (resume token / offset) and to process partial events (token delta vs structured events) in a robust, memory-friendly way. Current SDK helpers are low-level (raw bytes or event JSON) which pushes parsing and resume semantics into application code.

Proposed solution (high level):
1) EventSplitter: a small streaming parser that consumes the raw event stream (newline-delimited JSON and occasional binary frames) and yields typed event objects: "delta_token", "final_choice", "function_call", "tool_invocation", "heartbeat", "resume_marker". The splitter includes validation and noise-filtering (ignores empty heartbeats by default).

2) ResumeToken support: server will emit a stable resume_marker periodically (every N final choices or X tokens). The client stores the latest resume marker (opaque string). On reconnect, the client attaches resume_token in headers and the runtime will attempt to resume from that point. SDK exposes a single property on stream objects (stream.resume_token) and a helper method stream.resume_with(token).

3) Ergonomic API shapes: provide two main consumer patterns:
   - async iterator (preferred for "for await" style): async for event in client.chat.stream(...): handle(event)
   - callback router (for existing sync code): client.chat.stream(..., on_event=router_fn) which returns a small StreamHandle with cancel()/wait() methods.

4) Backpressure & memory safety: built on asyncio.Queue with configurable maxsize. Default builder uses conservative queue sizes and applies drop-oldest if application does not consume fast enough, with metric emission via console telemetry. We will expose flow-control knobs in the StreamOptions: max_buffered_events, drop_policy (drop_oldest|block_producer).

5) Retries & idempotency: streaming retries are best-effort; only resumptions using resume_token produce an idempotent continuation. Full-request retries (no token) will restart from the beginning. The SDK will surface a transparent RetryPolicy with backoff that prefers resume-based reconnect when token available.

Design tradeoffs considered:
- Resume granularity: token-per-message vs token-per-token. We used token-per-N-tokens balance to avoid emitting too many markers (cost + metadata footprint). Chosen default: resume every 64 tokens or on every final choice.
- API complexity vs power: we added two consumption patterns (iterator + callback) to support idiomatic usages; adding more shapes (observable streams, RxPy) was intentionally avoided for scope.
- Memory safety: drop_oldest may lose partial data — documented clearly and disabled in high-reliability defaults (block_producer).

Acceptance criteria:
- Streaming parser (EventSplitter) implemented and covered by unit tests (90% branch coverage on parsing edge cases).
- Resume flow tested end-to-end using local server harness that simulates network cut and confirms resume continues from last emitted token.
- Example notebooks and README updated with two idiomatic examples: async iterator and callback router.
- Metrics emitted: stream_resume_attempts, stream_resume_successes, stream_resume_failures, stream_queue_drops.
- API docs + migration guide published in docs/sdk/python/streaming-resume.md (internal link provided in comments).

Implementation notes:
- Files to add/modify: sdk/python/redwood_streaming.py, sdk/python/_events.py, tests/unit/test_streaming_resume.py, examples/streaming_resume.ipynb, docs/sdk/python/streaming-resume.md
- Use existing httpx.AsyncClient with keepalive; the streamer will wrap response.aiter_lines() with async generator that feeds EventSplitter.
- Use Pydantic models for typed events to simplify consumer code. Keep models minimal to avoid heavy runtime cost.

Testing plan:
- Unit: fuzz the newline-delimited event input with truncated JSON boundaries and unescaped characters.
- Integration: local harness (tools/local_stream_server) that supports two modes: immediate resume token emit and delayed markers. Create CI job that runs the harness + tests on linux/amd64 and macos-latest.

Documentation & examples:
- Add migration note: how to store resume_token safely (recommendation: persist after commit to DB or local disk, rotate token every X hours if using sensitive context).
- Provide example patterns for function-calling streams where app wants only final_choice events: stream.filter(EventType.FINAL_CHOICE).map(...). This will be a small helper on StreamHandle.

Rollout plan:
- Beta: enable resume by default but behind a feature flag in server and SDK (server-side opt-in). Ship SDK in beta channel and advertise in release notes.
- Monitor metrics for 2 weeks. If resume_success_rate < 85% for typical reconnections, revert and investigate.

Open questions:
- Should resume markers be signed (HMAC) to prevent tampering? (security raised this point in initial review). For now, treat markers as opaque and validate server-side. Follow-up security ticket recommended.
- How to handle partial function_call objects emitted across reconnects? We will re-emit full function_call only after the function_call is complete; partials are 'delta_token' events.
